card: Updates git-subtree-check.sh to verify that subtree merge commits are stacked directly on the previous subtree merge commit, allowing backports to release branches to reuse the exact same merge commit without a second round of review. The check can be bypassed with --incompatible when API breakage requires a newer base commit, which CI does by default to avoid false failures. This is a developer tooling and repository hygiene enhancement primarily benefiting backport maintainers and reviewers.
changed_since_previous: No substantial changes to the approach or diff; refactors command-line argument parsing and documents the practice in developer notes.
evidence: PR description: 'The exact same merge commit can then be reused on release branches, making the backport trivial to verify without rereviewing a newly generated subtree merge.'
problem: When subtree updates are based on newer commits on master rather than the previous subtree merge, the resulting merge commit cannot be reused verbatim when backporting to maintenance branches, forcing reviewers to inspect and verify a newly generated subtree merge for every release branch.

risk.why: Only touches repository linting scripts and documentation; a bug would only cause local subtree lint checks to report false positives or negatives.

summary: Updates test/lint/git-subtree-check.sh to check that the most recent subtree merge commit is stacked directly on the previous subtree merge commit. Adds an --incompatible flag to bypass this requirement when API changes require a newer base commit, and updates repo hygiene linting and developer documentation accordingly.
